thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: single-tenant performance anomaly detected for tenant=HighQ on pool=dedicated-us-west-2. p95/p99 SLO breach. Auto-pager to oncall.

samir (oncall): paging in — I saw the alert at 12:02 UTC. p95 jumped from ~0.45s -> ~3.2s, p99 from ~1.2s -> ~8.9s. Streaming responses are stalling mid-chunk for a subset of sessions (clients report partial responses then timeout). Only seeing errors for tenant HighQ. link to dashboard: https://dash.redwood/tenant/HighQ/latency (perf dash)

jess (eng-runtime): on it. Do we know if it's model-specific (redwood-x-large) or a runtime-level problem? Any difference between streaming vs non-streaming?

samir (oncall): looks concentrated on streaming. Non-streaming generation p95 is better but still elevated. Model=redwood-x-large (v12). GPU util looks fine from quick glance; suspect KV cache churn or request patterns.

datadog-bot: alert: 5xx_error_rate > 5% for tenant=HighQ (rules/tenant-errors).

maria (eng-sre): @samir please paste the top tail traces and a short sample of the stream logs. Also capture headroom on the dedicated pool (pending queue length, scheduler latencies).

samir (oncall): pasting clipped logs below — timestamps are relative to alert start:

```
[12:01:58] session=abc123 request_id=xyz789 stream_chunk=3 stall_detected=1 stall_duration=3500ms
[12:02:01] session=def456 request_id=xyz999 stream_chunk=1 stall_detected=1 stall_duration=4100ms
[12:02:12] gpu0_util=62% gpu1_util=58% queue_len=12 pending_batches=3 kv_cache_evictions=420
[12:02:16] model=redwood-x-large v=12 quant=fp16 tokens_sent=1200 tok/sec=300
```

These show repeated kv_cache_evictions spikes.

jess (eng-runtime): kv_cache_evictions jumping is a red flag. Do we have a pattern on prompt lengths / repeated prefix? HighQ recently rolled a long prompt template, right? @emily any customer changes?

emily (customer-success): confirmed: HighQ shipped a new interactive workflow yesterday that sends ~3k token prefixes per session and frequently reopens sessions. They've got high concurrency (~200 concurrent sessions). They're live. I'll ping their POC and warn them we're mitigating.

maria (eng-sre): mitigation options (short-term):
- route HighQ traffic to fallback model redwood-medium (faster, smaller KV needs)
- temporarily throttle per-session token throughput for HighQ (soft qps limit)
- enable prefix dedupe/cache for that tenant if possible
- if necessary, drain dedicated pool and failover to general pool (degrades isolation)

jess (eng-runtime): I can push a tenant-routing change to force fallback for HighQ. That is a config change to the traffic router; low risk but will change output distribution. Command I will run: 

```
# apply routing override for tenant HighQ -> redwood-medium (canary)
curl -X POST https://control.redwood/route-override \
  -d '{"tenant":"HighQ","model":"redwood-medium","mode":"canary","percent":100}' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN'
```

I can also flip an immediate rate-limit: `redwood rate-limit tenants HighQ --tps 50`

samir (oncall): please do the routing canary + 50 tps rate-limit now. I'll monitor.

ops-bot: Runbook invoked: TenantTailLatencyRunbook v2 — incident set to "mitigating". Paging eng-runtime lead.

jess (eng-runtime): applying routing override now (will post when done).

[~2m later]
jess (eng-runtime): routing change applied. rate-limit set. Returning deployment id: deploy-9247. Monitoring p95/p99.

samir (oncall): initial observations: p95 dropped from ~3.2s -> ~1.1s within 90s of change. p99 down to ~2.4s. Errors dropped from 5.2% -> 1.1%. Streaming stall count down ~70%. Dash snapshot: https://dash.redwood/incident/1768204567/snap

emily (customer-success): updating HighQ: "we're routing you to a fallback model to keep service available; may see brief differences in output. engineering is working on a targeted fix." Customer asked for ETA on restoration of baseline quality.

jess (eng-runtime): root cause hypothesis: heavy repeated prefixes + very long tokens per session causing KV cache thrash on the x-large model's per-shard KV capacity. The tenant's session pattern (3k token repeating context across many concurrent sessions) is evicting KV entries and causing frequent recomputation leading to stalls. Evidence: high kv_cache_evictions, correlation with token prefix size, tenant-only scope.

maria (eng-sre): next steps:
- create follow-up ticket with priority P1: increase tenant KV cap OR pin HighQ to a model variant with larger KV pool / enable persistent session cache.
- evaluate if we can enable prefix dedupe/cache at the proxy layer for long repeated prefixes.
- run a controlled repro with HighQ prompt shape in staging to confirm causal link.
- schedule a dedicated-capacity scaling window if kv growth is expected.

emily (customer-success): customer impact estimate: ~20% of requests saw degraded quality (due to fallback) while ~3% experienced timeouts prior to mitigation. They want root cause and a plan for restored latency + quality next week.

samir (oncall): declaring SLO breach for tenant HighQ for window 12:01-12:12 UTC. Recording for postmortem. Passing to night oncall for follow-up.

jess (eng-runtime): I'll open the PR to add per-tenant KV caps and a config toggle to enable prefix-dedupe. Also looking into increasing shard kv size for redwood-x-large but that requires a model bootstrap and can't be done live.

maria (eng-sre): please add a runbook step to auto-fallback to smaller model for tenants whose per-session tokens exceed 2000 tokens for more than 5 minutes. That will reduce future outages.

emily (customer-success): logged customer RCA request. Added them to a weekly sync.

samir (oncall): handing over to night oncall: @jess (eng-runtime) and @maria (eng-sre) to monitor. My notes: routing override applied (deploy-9247), rate-limit 50tps in place, observed p99 improved to ~2.4s. Follow-ups: ticket P1 -> KVSIZE-4321, repro task -> KVSIZE-4322, runbook change -> RUNBOOK-111.

jess (eng-runtime): ack. I'll run a controlled repro now and attach traces to KVSIZE-4322.

[~60m later]
jess (eng-runtime): follow-up update: repro shows same eviction pattern when we simulate 200 concurrent sessions with 3k prefix — confirmed. Two mitigations validated: (1) persistent session cache reduces evictions by 85% and (2) routing to redwood-medium reduces latency but loses some response quality. I'll put both mitigations in prioritization doc.

emily (customer-success): customer happy with mitigation for now but requested timeline for full fix.

maria (eng-sre): incident status -> mitigated, SLO breach recorded. Assigning postmortem to eng-runtime and eng-sre. Handoff complete.

samir (oncall): thanks team — closing active paging but leaving incident open for postmortem and action items. :thumbsup:
